summary: The reader has an undergraduate computer science education: asymptotic analysis and recurrences, discrete mathematics (sets, functions, permutations, modular arithmetic, primes, gcd), a first course in linear algebra (vectors, matrices, rank, bases, subspaces, orthogonality, dot products), complex numbers and polynomial algebra, and basic multitape Turing machine computation including binary arithmetic. They have seen schoolbook multiplication and basic divide-and-conquer, but not the FFT's number-theoretic refinements, abstract algebra beyond rings of polynomials, tensor products, bilinear forms over finite fields, or the analytic number theory used for prime estimates.

known.name: Logarithms and exponents
known.gloss: The base-2 logarithm and its rules (log of a product, powers and fractional exponents), including the ceiling form lg n and powers of log n such as (lg n)^(1-kappa).

known.name: Floor and ceiling functions
known.gloss: The functions that round a real number down or up to the nearest integer.

known.name: Binary and radix integer representation
known.gloss: An integer is written as a sequence of digits in a base, with value the sum of digit times power of the base, and addition propagates carries from low to high digits.

known.name: Schoolbook multiplication
known.gloss: The digit-by-digit multiplication algorithm taking time quadratic in the number of digits.

known.name: Modular arithmetic and congruences
known.gloss: Arithmetic on integers reduced to remainders modulo a fixed positive integer q, where a is congruent to b mod q when q divides a - b.

known.name: Primes, gcd and coprimality
known.gloss: Basic divisibility facts: primes, the gcd and coprimality of integers, the extended Euclidean algorithm giving Bezout coefficients and modular inverses, and primality testing by trial division.

known.name: Sets, functions, bijections and permutations
known.gloss: Standard discrete-mathematics vocabulary for finite sets, subsets, maps between them, one-to-one correspondences and rearrangements of an index set.

known.name: Counting and binomial coefficients
aliases: number of ones in a bit string
known.gloss: Counting subsets of a given size by binomial coefficients, and the Hamming weight of a bit string as its number of ones.

known.name: XOR and mod 2 arithmetic
known.gloss: Bitwise exclusive-or, which is addition of bits modulo 2 (so parity is the sum of bits mod 2).

known.name: Vectors, matrices and linear maps
known.gloss: Column vectors, matrix addition and multiplication, invertibility, and the view of a matrix as a linear map that acts on coordinate vectors.

known.name: Rank, bases and subspaces
known.gloss: Linear independence, bases, dimension of a subspace, the rank of a matrix as the dimension of its image, and row reduction by elementary operations.

known.name: Dot product and orthogonality
known.gloss: The dot product of vectors, perpendicularity when it is zero, orthonormal bases, and the orthogonal complement of a subspace.

known.name: Special matrices: triangular, diagonal and permutation matrices
known.gloss: Matrices with zeros above or below the diagonal, matrices that are diagonal, and 0-1 matrices with a single one in each row and column that permute coordinates.

known.name: Rational numbers and the number systems Q, R, C
known.gloss: The standard number systems of integers, rationals, reals and complex numbers, and arithmetic with fractions and denominators.

known.name: Roots of unity
known.gloss: The complex solutions of z^n = 1, equally spaced on the unit circle and given by powers of e^{2 pi i / n}.

known.name: Triangle inequality and absolute value
known.gloss: The inequality |a + b| <= |a| + |b| for absolute values and complex moduli, used with the maximum over entries to bound errors.

known.name: Geometric series and recurrences
known.gloss: Summing a geometric series, and solving or bounding running-time recurrences of divide-and-conquer algorithms by unrolling them.

known.name: Induction and proof by contradiction
known.gloss: Standard proof techniques from discrete mathematics: induction, contradiction and simple counting arguments.

known.name: Tape scans and constant-factor simulation on Turing machines
known.gloss: Basic multitape Turing machine programming: sweeping heads across a tape in linear time, copying data between tapes, and keeping bounded counters or carries in the finite control.

known.name: Schoolbook and Karatsuba-style divide-and-conquer multiplication
known.gloss: Multiplying integers by splitting them into pieces and recombining partial products, giving exponents below 2 such as n^{log_2 3}.

known.name: Polynomial evaluation and interpolation
known.gloss: Representing a polynomial by its coefficient list or its values at points, evaluating at a point, and reducing modulo a monic polynomial by remainder.

known.name: Newton iteration for reciprocals
known.gloss: Newton's method, which repeatedly refines an approximation to a root (such as a reciprocal) with roughly doubling precision at each step.
